bridge: Builds on S06 identity, F03 sandboxing and G02 privacy. This is a survey with one concrete permission exercise; advanced platform engineering requires the linked specialist material.
teaching:
Mobile platforms mediate app access through sandbox, permission, signing and distribution systems. A permission prompt is one layer: the app still needs a legitimate purpose, safe data handling and server-side authorisation. A signed package identifies a signing relationship, not a universal guarantee of benign behaviour.

Compare foreground access, background access and exported inter-app interfaces under the chosen platform's current rules. Those rules evolve, so use official documentation for exact API/version behaviour. Deep links and app-to-app messages create input boundaries similar to web requests.

The native exercise focuses on minimising data access for an invented note app. No phone rooting, malware installation or private data extraction is required. State what remains outside the survey: native code auditing, platform exploit development and complete store-compliance review need additional specialised study.
example:
Fictional offline notes app
Required function: write/read local text notes.
Proposed permissions: camera, microphone, contacts, precise location, network.
No feature uses these capabilities.
Decision: request none of them for the stated function.
If a later scan feature is added: request camera only when invoked,
explain purpose and retain a manual-entry path where feasible.
explanation: Permission need follows the feature and platform contract. “We might use it later” is not sufficient justification. A denied optional permission should not break unrelated note reading. Server data access remains separately scoped to the signed-in account.
exercise: Create a capability/purpose table for the app. Add a photo-attachment feature and define when access is requested, what data is retained and what happens after denial. Use the current official platform guide before claiming exact prompt behaviour.
solution: The basic app needs none of the listed unrelated permissions. Photo access should use the narrow platform-supported picker/capability when appropriate. Denial leaves core note functionality usable.
challenge: An exported deep link accepts note_id and account_id from another app. Explain the trust boundary and design checks preventing access to another user's note.
challenge_solution: Treat both fields as untrusted input; derive account identity from trusted session/platform state and authorise the target object. App signing and a valid link format do not prove the caller may select an arbitrary account.
